title: Add link-format and anchor-text configuration to LinkColumn
body:
### Problem

The current implementation of `st.column_config.LinkColumn` expects the column to have a URL as the value and the whole URL is displayed in cells. Often times these URLs may belong to the same domain and have the same path prefix while any meaningful differentiating piece of text appears after them. In such cases, it might be helpful to allow a way to format the displayed text while keeping the original link underneath as the value. Also, in some case the display text might be stored in a different column, like title of pages linked to their URLs. Moreover, the data of the column might not be in link format, but can be converted to a link on the fly.

### Solution

There are three requirements here that possibly be consolidated to only two:

1. Given a column with values like `1`, `2`, `3`... one might want to convert it to `https://example.com/docs/page_{}.html` using a plain format option or a function/lambda expression.
2. Given a column with values like `https://example.com/docs/page_1.html`, `https://example.com/docs/page_2.html`, `https://example.com/docs/page_3.html`... one might want to link these to simply their file names, such as `page_1.html`, `page_2.html`, `page_3.html`... using format function/lambda expression.
3. Given a column with values as links (or ones that can be formatted as links using option 1 above), one might want to use the value from another column as anchor-text using a display column name and/or formatting function/lambda expression that expects the whole row as a dict argument.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: For (1), I think we could just add `format_func` as a parameter, similar to how we have that on some widgets. I'm not sure we can do (2) at this point since I believe the underlying library needs to show the entire URL in the table and we can't show a different text.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: I think there might even be a 4th requirement: Show the same display label for all rows in a link column, e.g., `Open Website`.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
The big issue here is that we don't really want to modify the cells of the dataframe in the Python backend. Doing that would make a lot of things slow and complicated, especially in relation to editing support. So a  function/lambda expression would not work with `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor`. We probably need to find a way to configure a display label for `LinkColumn` in a way that the frontend can apply it. 

One possible solution could be: LinkColumn is always expected to contain the URL as cell value. To configure a display label, we add a `format` parameter to `LinkColumn` that allows setting a single display label (e.g. `LinkColumn(format="Open Website")`) or a regex pattern to extract a single display value from the cell value (e.g. `LinkColumn(format="^https:\/\/example\.com\/docs\/(.+)\.html$")`.

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
Hi @participant15,

Little bug with `display_text` here. It doesn't work for a combination of `st.dataframe` and pandas Styler.

Using the [original example](https://link-column.streamlit.app/), with some modifications:
```
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.dataframe(
    pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "col_0":
                [
                    "https://streamlit.io/",
                    "https://<redacted-host>/",
                    "https://streamlit.io/gallery",
                    None,
                ],
            "col_1":
                [
                    "https://roadmap.streamlit.app",
                    "https://extras.streamlit.app",
                    "https://issues.streamlit.app",
                    None,
                ],
            "col_2":
                [
                    "https://roadmap.streamlit.app",
                    "https://extras.streamlit.app",
                    "https://issues.streamlit.app",
                    None,
                ],
        }
    ).style.format(),
    column_config={
        "col_0":
            st.column_config.LinkColumn("Link column"),
        "col_1":
            st.column_config.LinkColumn(
                "Link with display text",
                display_text="View",
            ),
        "col_2":
            st.column_config.LinkColumn(
                "Link with regex extraction",
                display_text="^https://(.*?).streamlit.app$",
                validate="^https://.*?.streamlit.app$",
            ),
    },
)
```
Output: 
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/28784317/1eb29a63-891c-4e08-ab87-20c6e0e02c64)

Notes:
- It works perfectly if we use the default `st.data_editor` instead, for both ordinary pandas DataFrame and Styler.
- It only works for `st.dataframe` if we use ordinary DataFrame. `st.data_editor(disabled=True)` doesn't work as well.
